newsitem.title: USA: Foreigners bought more U.S. securities in Q3.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners bought more U.S. securities in Q3.

text.p: Foreign buying of marketable U.S. Treasury bonds and notes during the third quarter was nearly double the pace set during the second quarter, a Treasury Department report on Friday indicated.

Net foreign purchases by foreigners of long-term securities, reported by U.S. banks and brokers, jumped to $73.46 billion during the third quarter from $38.3 billion in the second quarter, according to the December Treasury Bulletin.

The heaviest volume of buying -- during the third quarter and for any month in the first three quarters of 1996 -- occurred during July when a net $47.83 billion of U.S. securities were bought by foreigners.
Buying in August totaled a net $11.87 billion while another $13.78 billion of long-term securities were purchased in September.

The Treasury counts on strong foreign demand for U.S. securities to finance huge government debts. Periodically, concern is raised that reduced foreign demand could put pressure on interest rates though that was not the case during the third quarter.
